content: Hydroxyzine is a medication prescribed to alleviate itching caused by allergic reactions. It is also used to manage nausea and vomiting associated with various conditions, including motion sickness. Additionally, it is prescribed to treat anxiety and symptoms related to alcohol withdrawal. In some cases, it may be used for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Hydroxyzine is available in several forms, including capsules, tablets, syrup, and suspension, all of which are taken orally. It is typically taken three or four times daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Do not administer this medication to children under 12 years of age unless specifically directed by a doctor. Before starting hydroxyzine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to hydroxyzine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs you are currently taking, especially antihistamines, medications for colds, allergies, or hay fever, antidepressants, seizure medications, muscle relaxants, narcotic pain relievers, sedatives, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, and vitamins. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking hydroxyzine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your surgeon or dentist that you are taking hydroxyzine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Additionally, alcohol can enhance the sedative effects of this drug, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. If you miss a dose of hydroxyzine, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Hydroxyzine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include dry mouth, nose, and throat; upset stomach; drowsiness; dizziness; chest congestion; headache; and skin redness. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, such as difficulty breathing, muscle weakness, or increased anxiety, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a severe reaction, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store hydroxyzine in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor while taking hydroxyzine. Do not share this medication with others. If you have any questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Hydroxyzine is sold under several brand names, including Anx®, Atarax®, Atarax® Syrup, and Vistaril®.
